abstract.p: An amplifier includes a first transistor (T1) whose emitter is connected to an amplifier output (Y) and whose collector is connected to a first (V<+>) of two current supply terminals (V<+>, V<->), wherewith the base of the first transistor (T1) is connected to an input (X). A constant load circuit (10) is connected between the emitter of the first transistor (T1) and the second current supply terminal (V<->). The constant load circuit (10) is adapted to ensure that the current through the first transistor (10) will always exceed a lowest value, so that the first transistor (T1) will always lie in a limited, generally linear area of its working curve.

Cet amplificateur comprend un premier transistor (T1), dont l'émetteur est connecté à une sortie d'amplificateur (Y) et dont le collecteur est connecté à une première borne (V<+>) d'une paire de bornes d'alimentation en courant (V<+>, V<->), la base du premier transistor (T1) étant connectée à une entrée (X). Un circuit de charge constante (10) est connecté entre l'émetteur du premier transistor (T1) et la seconde borne d'alimentation en courant (V<->). Le circuit de charge constante (10) est conçu pour assurer que le courant traversant le premier transistor (10) dépasse toujours une valeur la plus basse, de sorte que le premier transistor (T1) va toujours se situer dans une zone généralement linéaire limitée de sa courbe de travail.

description.p: The present invention relates to an amplifier of the kind defined in the preamble of the accompanying Claim 1.
A primary object of the invention is to provide an amplifier, particularly an audiofrequency amplifier which will reproduce true-to-life sound (speech, music, etc.).

Audiofrequency amplifiers are well known in semiconductor constructions, where great efforts have been made to provide lifelike sound reproduction. In practice, however, developments have not proceeded to any great extent, since tube amplifiers are still considered to provide splendid sound in comparison with semiconductor constructions.

Accordingly, an object of the present invention is to provide a semiconductor amplifier which while affording the advantages associated with a class-A amplifier will not have the dominant drawback of the class-A amplifier, namely poor efficiency.

For instance, true-to-life sound reproduction can be achieved with a tube-equipped class-A amplifier that includes a constant current generator (or a resistor) , by virtue of the fact that current amplification can be achieved in a small delimited area of the working curve of the current amplifying unit. This results in good linearity while eliminating any overtone distortions.

The inventive amplifier stage includes a first transistor whose emitter is connected to an amplifier output and whose collector is connected to a first of two current supply terminals, the base of the first transistor being connected to a signal input.
The invention is set forth in Claim 1. Further embodiments of the inventive amplifier will be apparent from the accompanying dependent Claims.

Thus, in order to achieve very pure sound of high transparency with such an amplifier at the same time as the efficiency of said amplifier is much greater than the efficiency of a class-A amplifier, the inventive amplifier shall be designed so as to include a sensing circuit (constant load circuit) between the emitter of the first transistor and the second output, and the sensing circuit shall be adapted to ensure that the current through the first transistor will always exceed a lowest value, so that the transistor will constantly lie in a delimited, generally linear area of its working curve.

In one embodiment of the invention, the emitter of the first transistor may be connected to the amplifier output via a first conductor part which includes a first resistance, wherewith a second conductor part is connected to the first conductor part in parallel and contains a second resistance and a diode in series therewith.

The constant load circuit includes a second transistor whose collector is connected to the second current supply terminal and whose emitter is connected to the load. The constant load circuit also includes a shunt line between the second current supply terminal and the emitter of the first transistor, wherewith the shunt line of the constant load circuit inclu- des an adjustable zener diode or a corresponding device which is set so that the diode of the second conductor part will not conduct when the amplifier idles. The input of the second transistor is connected to the shunt line between the second current supply terminal and the adjustable diode. A third transistor may be connected in the Darlington-arrangement with the second transistor in the constant load circuit. The
constant load circuit is adapted to ensure that current will continue to flow through the first resistance (resistor) of the first conductor part. A fourth transistor is suitably connected in a Darlington-arrangement with the first transistor, between said input and the first transistor. The constant load circuit is adapted to ensure that the first and the fourth transistor will continue to conduct even on the negative half of the output signal.
The invention will now be described in more detail by way of example with reference to the accompanying drawing.
Fig. 1 is a schematic illustration of an inventive amplifier.
Shown in Fig. 2 are two current supply terminals, namely

+supply and -supply, V+ and V" respectively. Also shown is an input line X to which an input signal is delivered. The illustration also includes an output line Y which delivers an output signal via a load indicated by resistance R . Two transistors Tl, T2 are connected in a Darlington-arrangement in a conductor path 1, 2, 3 between the +supply V+ and the output Y.

The conductor path includes three mutually sequential conductor sections 1, 2 and 3, wherewith the transistors Tl, T2 are connected on the conductor section 1 (the transistor T2 being controlled by the input X and controlling the transistor Tl). The conductor section 2 includes a resistance Rl . A conductor section 5, which is parallel with the conduc- tor section 2, includes a resistance R2 in series with a diode Dl . R2, Dl are adapted to ensure that the voltage drop across Rl will not be excessively large in the event of a positive swing. The conductor section 2 is connected to the -supply V" by a conductor section 6. A shunt line 7 is arranged parallel with the conductor sections 2 and 6. As seen in a direction away from the -supply V", the conductor
section 7 includes a resistance R3 and then an adjustable diode D2 that includes a parallel-connected capacitance Cl. Two transistors T3, T4 are connected in a Darlington- arrangement in the conductor section 6, wherewith the transistor T4 is controlled via an input line 8 from the conductor section 7 between the diode D2 and the resistance R3. D2 is selected so that Dl will not conduct when the amplifier idles. When the signal on the input X is below 0 volts, the constant load circuit 10 (D2, T4, T3) ensures that current continues to flow through Rl . Thus, Tl, T2 will continue to conduct even on the negative half period of the output.

The constant load 10 ensures that the transistor Tl can handle the second polarity on the output Y. Thus, as a result of the inventive constant load 10 the occurrent loss in efficiency is limited by ensuring that the current through the transistor Tl will always exceed a lowest value. Due to this current, the transistor Tl will always lie in a small restricted area of its working curve. This results in good linearity with respect to power gain and eliminates or minimises the transition distortion so as to enable such distortion to be ignored. One advantage afforded by the inventive amplifier is that the components required are far fewer than those required in a conventional amplifier stage. Another advantage is that the inventive amplifier will nevertheless produce absolutely pure sound with a very high degree of transparency. The illustrated circuit includes bipolar transistors, although the person skilled in this art will realise that other types of semiconductors can be used.

claim.claim-text: 1. An amplifier which includes a first transistor (Tl) whose emitter is connected to an amplifier output (Y) and whose collector is connected to a first (V+) of two current supply terminals (V+, V") , wherewith the base of the first transistor (Tl) is connected to an input (X) , characterised in that a constant load circuit (10) is connected between the emitter of the first transistor (Tl) and the second current supply terminal (V~) ; and in that the constant load circuit (10) is adapted to ensure that the current through the first transistor (10) will always exceed a lowest value, so that the first transistor (Tl) will always lie in a limited, generally linear area of its working curve.

2. An amplifier according to Claim 1, characterised in that the emitter of the first transistor (Tl) is connected to the amplifier output (Y) via a conductor path (2, 3) which includes a first resistance (Rl) ; and in that a conductor part (5) connected in parallel to the first resistance (Rl) includes in series a second resistance (R2) and a first diode (Dl) which conducts current in a direction towards the output (Y) •

3. An amplifier according to Claim 1 or 2, characterised in that the constant load circuit (10) includes second transistor (T3) whose collector is connected to the second current supply terminal (V") and whose emitter is connected to said output; in that the constant load circuit (10) also includes a shunt line (7) between the second current supply terminal (V") and the emitter of the first transistor (Tl) , wherewith the shunt line (7) of the constant load circuit (10) includes an adjustable diode (D2) which is set so that the diode (Dl) of the conductor part (5) will not conduct when the amplifier idles; and in that the input (8) of the second transistor (T3) is connected to the shunt line (7)' between the second current supply terminal (V) and the adjustable diode (D2) .

4. An amplifier according to Claim 3, characterised in that the shunt line (7) includes a third resistance (R3) between the second current supply terminal (V") and the adjustable diode (D2); and in that the input (8) of the second transistor (T3) is connected to the shunt line (7) between the third resistance (R3) and the adjustable diode (D2) .
5. An amplifier according to Claim 3 or 4, characterised in that a third transistor (T4) is connected in Darlington- arrangement with the second transistor (T3) in the load circuit (10) .
6. An amplifier according to any one of Claims 3-5, characterised in that the load circuit is adapted to ensure that current will continue to flow through the first resistance (Rl) .

7. An amplifier according to any one of Claims 1-6, characterised in that a fourth transistor (T2) is connected in Darlington arrangement with the first transistor (Tl) between the input (X) and the first transistor (Tl) .

8. An amplifier according to any one of Claims 1-7, characterised in that the constant load circuit (10) is adapted to ensure that the first and the fourth transistors (Tl, T2) will continue to conduct even on the negative period parts of the output.
